basis: Nothing filed: items 0-1 sit outside the window and 2-7 are searched-and-found-nothing; annual reports have not moved this stock (item 3).
against: An annual report can still carry a going-concern or capex note, but nothing in the pack points to one.

basis: No finding; the annual report restates a public balance sheet and the runway is long (items 2-6).
against: The unexplained -26% drawdown could keep running, but nothing dated drives it inside the window.

basis: Directors bought after the guide cut (item 2) and a long holder is accumulating (item 3); both suggest the H2 bar is beatable (item 1).
against: The half was pre-released, and the two previous interims both fell 2-3% (item 0); reiterating the guide is the base case, and it carries no news.

basis: The run-up came from a broker note on the Meta settlement that the company cannot validate (item 0), and the FY revenue bar needs H2 to reverse its trend (item 1).
against: EBITDA has been sandbagged and looks beatable at 4x EV/EBITDA (item 2), and this name has paid for EBITDA beats before.

basis: The company itself committed to a Lockers review update at this release (item 0), and it pre-disclosed Q2 bookings up more than 20%, which lowers the odds of a guide cut (item 1).
against: The modal update is 'process continues', the hardware decline (item 3) puts the Lockers margin target at risk, and the last two H1/FY prints fell around 15%.

basis: Flat Q2 comps on rising SG&A point to Q2 OP falling year on year (item 0), the same line that took the stock down 9.5% last year; margin longs are crowded.
against: September comps of +10.4% (item 1) give management a strong H2 narrative, and the monthlies are already public to Japanese readers.

basis: Interest coverage sits near the 2.0x covenant floor at the June test (item 2), the Nasdaq bid cure cannot complete in time (item 1), and no FY27 guide is likely while the review runs (item 0).
against: The stock already fell 20% in five days with no news (item 3), and any refinancing headline could squeeze a 14%-short nano-cap; the coverage arithmetic is my inference and could be a full turn wider.

basis: The CEO's 10b5-1 buying stopped and the price bid went with it (item 0), and there is an unexplained Q1 cash drain on a negative-equity balance sheet (item 1).
against: The stock is already down 44% in 20 days; a decent billings print on a thin float could bounce it hard.

basis: Revenue is flat sequentially behind the YoY headline (item 2), the funding narrative is doubtful: an unverifiable lender (item 1) and in-quarter ATM sales (item 4), and governance is weak (item 3); the last two earnings reactions were -18% and -20%.
against: If the $30m facility is validated on the call, it removes the going-concern overhang, and the market has given it zero value.

basis: A forwarding upcycle hit the June quarter after the stale consensus was set (item 0), and the stock beat stale consensus on the last two prints with +9.8% and +16.3%.
against: The brokerage margin squeeze offsets it (item 1), and the company's own mix cannot be weighed, so the forwarding gain may not show.

basis: ORLY's July step-up and the record-hot August fall in AZO's quarter but after AAP's (item 0), the LIFO comp is easy (item 1), and calls are bid.
against: Six of the last seven prints fell, including on comp beats; the weather inference has not paid in the past, and the gross-margin line could still disappoint.

basis: The cost restructuring (item 2) and the lean dealer lots (item 3) at the guide-setting print, with ~10 days to cover on the short and the stock near its low.
against: German motorhome registrations collapsed (item 0) and revenue consensus sits above the guide (item 1), so a weak FY27 Europe guide is just as plausible.

basis: No filed finding; the extra workday and fuel were checked and are priced or immaterial (items 2-3).
against: Commentary on the FTC deal timing could move it, but the sign is unknowable.

basis: Record sponsorship deals signed after the last guide feed a FY27 guide (item 1), on the line that paid +12.7%, with a heavily shorted thin float (item 2).
against: Q4 consensus sits above the guide-implied maximum, the same shape that produced last year's -7% miss (item 0), and the higher interest cost (item 3).

basis: The Q4 guide will be struck at spot Brent near $106, implying roughly $0.10-0.13 of EPS against a Street Q4 figure that only took $0.07 out (item 1), and the guide is the line this stock trades on.
against: Fuel is in every preview and the stock is down 15% on it; a Q3 beat (item 0) plus strong close-in demand and an upside-paid skew could carry the print.

basis: The trust data shows no new credit deterioration (item 0), and units likely clear an easy revenue bar (item 1).
against: This stock has sold off on beats; depreciation during the quarter pressures GPU (item 2), and 6 of the last 8 prints fell hard.

basis: A likely goodwill impairment at the year-end test (item 0) and freight pressure on the FY27 margin guide (item 1); the guidance line produced the -13.7% and -10.5% falls.
against: An impairment is non-cash and the market already values the company at half of book; the freight risk is macro inference.

basis: Every item was searched and dropped as priced or unsourced (items 0-6).
against: Freight and diesel could force a guide cut, but that is in the wire and in the 13% September fall.

basis: Run-rate ASV and revenue land at or above the top of the guide (item 0), into a moderately crowded short after a -17.5% narrative-driven slide.
against: The FY27 margin/EPS guide decides the reaction, and it sank the last Q4 print by 10% despite record ASV; the quarter beat is mostly priced.

basis: Management said on the call that IEEPA refunds had arrived and more were expected, with no filing showing them yet (items 0, 3); peers booking refunds this summer jumped 10-24%, the Q3 EPS bar is cut to about $0.11-0.13, and Q2 written sales back the revenue line (item 1).
against: The refund could be small, deferred or excluded from adjusted figures pending the auditors' view, and a thin, illiquid tape can do anything.
